title: Design Patterns in PHP
subtopics: Choosing patterns based on actual requirements.
learning_outcomes: Explain what design patterns in php contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: strategy.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Application architecture separates incoming requests, use-case rules, persistence, and external services. Patterns are useful when they clarify a dependency or invariant, not merely because they have a name. In this lesson, focus on strategy; then compare it with adapter. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use design patterns in php when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Application architecture separates incoming requests, use-case rules, persistence, and external services. Patterns are useful when they clarify a dependency or invariant, not merely because they have a name. For design patterns in php, begin with strategy. Also distinguish adapter; decorator; observer. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Design Patterns in PHP
content_blocks.code:
<?php
final class PriceCalculator { public function total(int $price, int $quantity): int { return $price * $quantity; } }
echo (new PriceCalculator())->total(12, 3) . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for design patterns in php from top to bottom. Start by identifying strategy, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for design patterns in php that demonstrates "strategy". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of strategy.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
